title: Arbitrated Economics Control Plane — initiative tracking for dynamic batching, caching, and quantization
creator: Maya K. Singh
description: Goal: Build an 'Arbitrated Economics Control Plane' (AECP) that provides declarative policies and automated orchestration to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs. AECP combines lightweight per-route policies, experiment toggles, and a cost-aware decision engine that selects batching, cache usage, and quantization profiles at inference time. This ticket tracks the PM-level initiative: OKRs, cross-team milestones, success metrics, risks, and rollout plan.
okrs: O1: Reduce average per-token serving cost by 18% across top 10 customer workloads by end of Q3 2026
KR1.1: Deploy AECP to 60% of hosted traffic (by route weighting) with automated fallbacks
KR1.2: Decrease long-tail 95th percentile token CPU/GPU cost by 25% for batched routes
KR1.3: Achieve <2% quality regressions (evaluated via prompt-suites) from quantized profiles
O2: Improve developer trust and adoption
KR2.1: Add per-route explainability logs and cost-breakdown to Console for 100% of routes using AECP
KR2.2: Run three customer pilots with Dedicated teams and gather qualitative adoption feedback
milestones: 2025-11-30: Spec approved (policy schema + decision engine interfaces)
2026-02-15: Core control plane prototype (simulator + API) merged
2026-03-20: First internal canary (non-customer hosted traffic) with batching policies
2026-05-31: Quantization profiles integrated and eval harness for regressions ready
acceptance_criteria: Declarative policy schema v1 accepted by Engineering and Design
Decision engine selects among at least 3 actions (no-change, batch-enlarge, quantize-profile) and logs chosen rationale per request
Rollout supports canary weights and automated rollback on quality regressions
Console exposes per-route cost delta and token-level attribution for AECP decisions
Automated evals run daily on canonical prompt suites with alerting on >2% regression
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Kickoff with Eng infra, Runtime, Console, and Research. Aligned on policy primitives and dataset requirements.
2025-12-18: Decisions taken to keep policy schema lightweight (route-level predicates + request-context hints). Trade-off: more conservative actions initially to reduce risk.
2026-01-25: Prototype decision engine implemented (rule-based + lightweight cost estimator). Shared integration PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1897
2026-02-28: Engineering reported 12% avg savings in simulator for sampled workloads when enabling batching policies. Noted 1.8% quality drift on aggressive quant profiles—research to tune thresholds.
2026-03-05: Design feedback: Console cost visualization needs per-token waterfall and decision rationale modal. UX spike planned for 2026-03-18.
2026-03-10: Security review intake submitted (KMS implications for profile artifacts). Security requested key-rotation checklist and SOPs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions due to quantization. Mitigation: strict canary, automatic rollback, daily evals and conservative default profiles.
Risk: Added latency when decision engine runs per-request. Mitigation: decision caching + async decision retrieval with safe default action.
Risk: Cross-team coordination overhead (Runtime, Console, Research). Mitigation: weekly sync + dedicated eng liaison and clear API contracts.
Risk: Compliance for private deployments. Mitigation: ensure AECP control plane can operate in VPC-only mode and store profiles in customer KMS.
notes: We intentionally separate policy evaluation from heavy model operations — decisions should be O(1) and cacheable.
Conservative rollout principle: enable only single-dimension actions early (batching OR caching) before combining with quantization.
Experiment design: each canary will run randomized A/B (80/20) with instrumentation to estimate cost delta and QA signal within 48 hours.
Follow-ups: define 'cost credit' governance for teams experimenting with AECP to avoid destabilizing billing metrics.
customer_communications_plan: Phase 0: Internal customers + docs (engineering org) - April 2026
Phase 1: Invited pilots (top 5 customers by traffic) - June 2026
Phase 2: Gradual opt-in public beta with in-console toggles - Q3 2026
